text:
lucy_infra: Noticing a weird surge of tiny GPU pods Pending in ap-southeast1-a after the preemptive drain rollout. Lots of half-filled nodes (0.5 GPU used) and the scheduler refuses to pack new 0.125 GPU jobs on them. Users seeing timeouts.

ryan_qa: Saw failing e2e flakiness too. Logs show preemptions fired then kube-scheduler marking nodes as "Insufficient cpu/memory" for tiny pods even when GPU allocatable is available.

sam_ops: Paste a `kubectl describe` for one of the pods and the node status?

lucy_infra: snippet below from a pending pod:

```
Events:
  Type    Reason            Age   From               Message
  ----    ------            ----  ----               -------
  Warning FailedScheduling  14m   default-scheduler  0/36 nodes are available: 20 node(s) had taint "preempt/soon:NoSchedule" that the pod didn't tolerate, 16 node(s) had insufficient memory, 36 node(s) Insufficient ephemeral-storage.
```

ryan_qa: And node allocatable show: `nvidia.com/gpu: 1`, `cpu: 8`, `memory: 30Gi` but we are reserving 4Gi per GPU slot in the kubelet reservation. That reservation was increased last week for stability during high-load model loading. For tiny pods that reservation is overkill and causes the "Insufficient memory" symptom.

devon_scheduler: The scheduler's binpacking comparator currently sorts by "most requested resources first" which causes it to avoid filling fragmented nodes when there is a slight memory reservation. There's also a preemption hook that marks nodes tainted with `preempt/soon=true` during drain windows. Combined effects: small jobs see both taint and perceived memory shortage.

sam_ops: Two paths: reduce kubelet static reservation per GPU or change scheduling logic to prefer filling nodes with existing GPU allocations (i.e., allow multi-tenant small pods on same GPU card) using PodTopologySpread and a new scoring plugin. Which is lower risk?

lucy_infra: For immediate relief, can we do a temporary mutating webhook that adds toleration for `preempt/soon:NoSchedule` and a label check so only jobs annotated `redwood/small-burst=true` get it? That plus lowering reservation on warmpool nodes should get most running.

devon_scheduler: Webhook + reservation tweak is fine as short-term. Long-term we should: 1) implement fractional packing support in the scheduler scoring (weight GPUs higher than memory for GPU-bound pods), 2) add a preemption grace window so nodes in drain don't immediately taint, and 3) introduce per-pod reservation override for tiny executor containers.

evict-bot: auto-note: created incident INC-2026-33 for "ap-southeast1 tiny GPU pending spike" and assigned to eng-platform. See https://incidents.internal/INC-2026-33

ryan_qa: I ran a quick sim in staging switching reservation from 4Gi->1Gi for warmpool nodes. Pending count dropped 78% for tiny pods. No regressions seen in model loads.

sam_ops: Let's roll the reservation change in a canary across one AZ first. Also enable the webhook in staging for 30m and monitor preemptions.

lucy_infra: I'll prepare the webhook manifest and tests. We should also add an alert metric: ratio(tiny_pods_pending / tiny_pods_total) > 0.2 for 5m per AZ to catch early.

devon_scheduler: Filed follow-up PR: scheduler will get fractional-packing-scoring and a toggle `enableFractionalPacking` behind a feature flag. Planning doc: https://go/internal/scheduler/fractional-packing.

sam_ops: Rolling reservation change to canary now. Will update this thread when canary completes.

lucy_infra: Thanks. If canary looks good, schedule broader rollout during off-peak. Also add an action item to review kubelet eviction thresholds so ephemeral-storage claims don't hide as memory shortages.

sam_ops: Canary green: tiny pending down from 120->22 in canary AZ. No NVLink or model load OOMs observed. Rolling to rest of region in 15m.

ryan_qa: Nice. Adding a test to our CI that creates 200 0.125 GPU pods to ensure scheduler packing behavior doesn't regress.

lucy_infra: Closing thread after follow-ups are tracked in the backlog. Follow-ups: webhook, reservation tweak rollout, scheduler feature flag PR, alert rule, CI test. Thanks everyone. :party:
